title: Programming with Quantum-Controlled Quantum Channels
summary: In contrast to a classical bit, which can only take the value $0$ or $1$, its quantum counterpart -- a qubit -- can exist in a superposition of $0$ and $1$. This is a superposition of data values, naturally raising the question of whether one can superpose not only data but also programs. For example, a particular superposition of programs, known as the quantum SWITCH, has attracted much attention, and its implementations and computational advantages have been studied extensively within the physics community. A naive way to control a program by a qubit is by means of a controlled operation.…
